Average Cost for 1-800-GOT-JUNK? in Jacksonville FL

If you’re staring at a mountain of unwanted stuff in Jacksonville, you’re probably wondering, “How much will 1-800-GOT-JUNK? actually charge me?” The good news is that the company is transparent about its pricing, and you can get a solid estimate in just a few clicks. Below, we break down the typical price range, the factors that can shift the cost up or down, and some savvy tips to keep your wallet happy.

How 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Prices Are Calculated

Unlike many local junk haulers that quote by the hour, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? uses a volume‑based model. The crew measures the amount of space your junk occupies in a standard 8‑ft truck, then applies a per‑cubic‑yard rate that varies by city.

  • Flat‑rate pricing: You’ll receive a single, all‑inclusive figure that covers labor, disposal fees, and cleanup.
  • No hidden charges: There are no extra fees for stairs, distance, or “heavy items” – everything is bundled.
  • Online estimates: The website’s calculator lets you input the items you have and instantly generates an estimate.

Because the pricing is based on volume, the exact cost depends on how much space your junk takes up, not just the weight or type of items.

Typical Price Ranges in Jacksonville

In Jacksonville, the average cost for a full‑truck load (about 10‑12 cubic yards) falls between $300 and $400. Here’s a quick look at the most common scenarios:

Small Load (1‑2 cubic yards)

Perfect for a single room cleanout or a handful of old furniture. Expect to pay $100‑$150.

Medium Load (3‑5 cubic yards)

Ideal for a garage cleanout, partial home renovation debris, or a sizable yard waste job. Prices typically range from $180‑$250.

Large Load (6‑10 cubic yards)

When you’re tackling a whole‑house declutter or a major remodel, you’ll be looking at $300‑$400.

Extra‑Large Load (11+ cubic yards)

For commercial properties or extensive construction waste, the cost can climb beyond $500, but most residential projects stay below this threshold.

Remember, these figures are averages. Your final bill could be slightly lower or higher based on the specific items you have and any promotional discounts that may be running.

Factors That Can Influence the Final Cost

While the volume is the primary driver, a few other elements can tweak the price:

  • Item type: Hazardous materials (asbestos, chemicals) are not accepted, but bulky items like appliances are included at no extra charge.
  • Location within Jacksonville: Properties far from the main service hub may see a modest mileage surcharge, though 1-800-GOT-JUNK? usually absorbs this cost.
  • Seasonal demand: Spring and summer are peak moving seasons, so rates can be a bit higher during those months.
  • Special promotions: The company often runs discounts for first‑time customers, military personnel, or referrals.
